answer: Bind every agent to a hardware key. On joining, an agent must sign a fresh challenge with a TPM or secure-enclave key whose vendor certificate proves it is a real chip, and the ledger records a hash of that key. One chip can back only one active identity, so faking an atlas of a thousand agents means buying a thousand machines. Each epoch the network sends a random pulse that must be re-signed by the same chip within seconds, so keys cannot be lent around. A sybil plume shrinks to the number of devices an attacker actually owns.
